case_title: Puran Chand v. State of H.P.
trial_court_outcome: Convicted and sentenced to 7 years RI
neutral_facts: The accused was alleged to have committed rape on a minor girl. The victim, who was 17 years old at the time of the incident, attempted suicide after the alleged rape and later disclosed the incident to her family and the police. The victim's family reported the case to the police, leading to the registration of an FIR. The victim underwent medical examination, and the medical report indicated that her hymen was intact. The accused was arrested and charged under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code. The trial court convicted the accused and sentenced him to seven years of rigorous imprisonment along with a fine of Rs. 5,000. The High Court upheld the conviction and sentence. The accused appealed, arguing that the delay in lodging the FIR and the medical evidence undermined the prosecution's case. The Supreme Court examined the evidence, including the victim's testimony, the delay in reporting the incident, and the trauma experienced by the victim. The Court found the prosecution's case credible, noting that the delay in reporting the incident and the victim's suicide attempt supported her account of the rape. The Court also emphasized that the amendment to Section 114-A of the Evidence Act supported the prosecution's case, even in the absence of clear medical evidence of rape.
